organic_wet.handling_summary: Compost or biogas plant. Do not mix with dry waste.

items.name: Banana Peel
recycling_steps: Collect in green bin
Transfer to compost bin or biogas unit
Can be used as natural fertilizer after composting
items.handling_tips: Ideal for vermicomposting. Rich in potassium.

items.name: Food Scraps
recycling_steps: Segregate in green lidded bin
Transport to municipal composting facility
Convert to compost or biogas
items.handling_tips: Avoid putting oily or salted food in compost bins. Use bokashi for cooked food.

items.name: Garden Waste
recycling_steps: Collect in green bin or biodegradable bag
Shred for faster composting
Mix with kitchen scraps for balanced compost
items.handling_tips: Excellent carbon source for compost pile. Avoid chemically treated plants.

items.name: Egg Shells
recycling_steps: Rinse and dry
Crush and add to compost for calcium boost
Can be used directly as soil amendment
items.handling_tips: Crushed eggshells deter garden pests. Excellent compost additive.

items.name: Tea Bags
recycling_steps: Remove staple if present
Add to compost directly
Loose-leaf tea is fully compostable
items.handling_tips: Plastic-mesh tea bags should go to general waste. Prefer paper-only bags.

recyclable_dry.handling_summary: Clean, dry, and segregate by material type before placing in blue bin.

items.name: Plastic Bottle
recycling_steps: Rinse thoroughly to remove residue
Remove cap and label if possible
Crush to save bin space
Place in blue recycling bin
Sorted at MRF into PET/HDPE streams
Shredded into flakes and pelletized for reuse
items.handling_tips: Never place oily or contaminated bottles in recycling. Caps are recyclable separately.

items.name: Cardboard Box
recycling_steps: Flatten to reduce volume
Remove tape and staples
Keep dry — wet cardboard loses recyclability
Place in blue bin or paper collection point
items.handling_tips: Pizza boxes with grease stains are not recyclable. Tear off clean sections.

items.name: Glass Bottle
recycling_steps: Rinse clean
Remove metal lids separately
Do not break — whole bottles are easier to sort
Place in glass-specific collection bin
items.handling_tips: Coloured glass (amber, green) must be separated from clear glass at advanced facilities.

items.name: Aluminium Can
recycling_steps: Rinse to remove sugary residue
Crush flat
Place in metals bin or blue recycling bin
Melted at 660°C and re-cast — infinite recyclability
items.handling_tips: Aluminium recycling uses 95% less energy than virgin production. Always recycle cans.

items.name: Newspaper
recycling_steps: Bundle and tie with twine
Keep dry and clean
Drop at paper collection drive or blue bin
items.handling_tips: Shredded paper can be added to compost as a carbon source.

items.name: Steel Scrap
recycling_steps: Separate from non-metal materials
Place in metals collection bin
Sent to scrap dealer or steel mill for smelting
items.handling_tips: Steel is 100% recyclable. Avoid mixing with contaminated waste.

e_waste.handling_summary: Never put in regular bins. Deposit at certified e-waste kiosks or registered dismantlers.

items.name: Smartphone
recycling_steps: Perform factory reset and wipe personal data
Remove SIM and memory cards
Deposit at OEM take-back program or certified e-waste kiosk
Dismantler recovers gold, silver, palladium from PCB
Battery sent to Li-ion recycling facility
items.handling_tips: Never dispose in regular bins. Contains toxic cadmium, lead, and mercury. Data wiping is mandatory.

items.name: Laptop
recycling_steps: Backup and securely wipe all data (DoD 5220.22-M standard)
Remove battery for separate handling
Deposit at manufacturer take-back or certified dismantler
Precious metals recovered via hydrometallurgy
items.handling_tips: Consider refurbishing and donating before disposal. Many NGOs accept functional laptops.
items.regulatory_note: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance mandatory under CPCB India.

items.name: CRT Monitor
recycling_steps: Do not break — lead-bearing glass is hazardous
Contact certified CRT dismantler only
Lead glass sent to smelters for safe processing
items.handling_tips: CRT monitors contain 4–8 lbs of lead. Illegal to landfill in most jurisdictions.
items.regulatory_note: Classified as hazardous waste. Requires manifest tracking per Hazardous Waste Rules.

items.name: Printer Cartridge
recycling_steps: Return via retailer take-back program (HP, Canon, etc.)
Or drop at e-waste collection drive
Remanufacturing possible for most cartridge types
items.handling_tips: Many office supply stores offer free cartridge recycling drop-off.

items.name: Lithium Battery
recycling_steps: Never puncture or crush
Store in fire-proof bag if damaged
Drop at battery recycling point or e-waste facility
Hydrometallurgical recovery of lithium, cobalt, nickel
items.handling_tips: Damaged Li-ion batteries are fire hazards. Never place in general waste or recycling bins.
items.regulatory_note: Aviation and transport restrictions apply to lithium batteries.

toxic_hazardous.handling_summary: Requires special handling. Contact municipal hazardous waste facility or certified disposal agent.

items.name: Paint
recycling_steps: Leave lid off to dry out latex paint (acceptable for solid disposal)
Never pour down drain — contaminates groundwater
Bring to household hazardous waste (HHW) collection event
Unopened paint can be donated to community reuse programs
items.handling_tips: Oil-based paint is more hazardous than latex. Store away from heat sources.

items.name: Motor Oil
recycling_steps: Collect in sealed, labelled container
Never mix with other chemicals
Take to auto shop or municipal oil recycling depot
Re-refined into base oil or used as fuel supplement
items.handling_tips: One litre of motor oil can contaminate 1 million litres of drinking water.

items.name: Fluorescent Tube
recycling_steps: Handle with care — do not break
Place in original box or padded bag
Drop at retailer take-back or HHW facility
Mercury recovered via retort distillation
items.handling_tips: If broken indoors, ventilate immediately. Mercury vapour is toxic. Use gloves for cleanup.

items.name: Pesticide Container
recycling_steps: Triple-rinse container
Puncture to prevent reuse
Return to AgriShop or agricultural waste collection
Follow local pesticide disposal regulations
items.handling_tips: Never burn pesticide containers. Fumes are highly toxic. Triple-rinse is mandatory.

items.name: Medical Sharps
recycling_steps: Place immediately in puncture-resistant sharps container
Never recap needles
Seal container when 3/4 full
Return to pharmacy, clinic, or mail-back sharps program
items.handling_tips: Loose needles in bins are a public health and safety risk. Always use sharps containers.
items.regulatory_note: Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016 — Yellow/Red category disposal mandated.
